explanation: HMP pathway's main importance in brain is generating NADPH for antioxidant defense (via glutathione reductase) and nucleotide synthesis; NADPH protects against oxidative stress which is critical for neurons.
Hormones and neurotransmitters are signal molecules for cell-cell communication, derived from amino acids (nitrogenous) but also include non-nitrogenous compounds like steroid hormones.
Glycine, glutamic acid (glutamate), and GABA are all amino acid neurotransmitters; glycine and GABA are inhibitory, glutamate is excitatory.
GABA is produced by decarboxylation of glutamic acid via glutamate decarboxylase (GAD), requiring PLP (vitamin B6) as cofactor; both a and c are correct.
All statements about amino acid neurotransmitters are true: glutamate is excitatory, glycine/GABA are inhibitory; glycine is in collagen; glutamate produces MSG; all above is correct.
Catecholamines (dopamine, norepinephrine, epinephrine) function as both hormones (adrenal medulla) and neurotransmitters (CNS/autonomic nervous system); both a and b are true.
Catecholamines contain the catechol (3,4-dihydroxyphenyl) ring and are synthesized from tyrosine (not glycine); tyrosine hydroxylase is the rate-limiting enzyme.
L-DOPA is produced from tyrosine by tyrosine hydroxylase (not from dopamine); dopamine is synthesized from L-DOPA by DOPA decarboxylase. Option D (neither) is correct.
Tyrosine hydroxylase catalyzes the rate-limiting step by hydroxylating tyrosine to form DOPA; both formation of DOPA and hydroxylation of tyrosine describe the same step.
